To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

we have developed a mechanism to accelerate convolutional neural networks on CPU-FPGA shared memory systems by exploiting frequency domain acceleration, data layout optimization, and concurrent processing.
We present a novel FFT and OaA-based acceleration technique for convolutional layers in CNNs on CPU-FPGA system.
we propose a novel FFT-based acceleration of convolutional neural networks on a CPU-FPGA system.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the acceleration of CNNs on a CPU-FPGA platform.
the design and implementation of efficient and flexible FPGA-based accelerators for Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) inference.

the following aspects: (1) we exploit the FFT and OaA algorithms to accelerate convolutional layer in CNNs; (2) we design a 2D OaA-based convolution accelerator for FPGA; (3) we propose a novel memory layout to reduce data remapping overhead and sustain peak performance; (4) we design an efficient data transfer mechanism for CPU-FPGA system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the proposed approach achieves significant performance improvement over state-of-art CNN implementations.
our design achieves 3x ~ 5x speedup for the three networks over the state-of-the-arts.
our design is the first to exploit the FFT/OaA technique to accelerate the CNNs on CPU-FPGA shared memory system.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have achieved 1.35X GFLOPs/sec acceleration for AlexNet, 1.66X for VGG16 and 5.56X for GoogLeNet compared to the state-of-the- art implementations on the CPU platform.
we propose a novel mechanism to efficiently accelerate CNN on a shared memory platform.
we propose a novel mechanism to efficiently accelerate state-of-the-art Convolutional neural Networks on CPU-FPAG shared memory system with high performance and low resource consumption.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the frequency domain algorithms can accelerate convolutional layers on CPU-FPGA shared memory platform.

FFT and OaA-based convolution can significantly reduce the computational requirements for convolutional layers and can be efficiently mapped onto the FPGA with a high performance and low latency shared memory system.
FFT-based acceleration of convolutional layer on CPU-FPGA shared memory platform is very efficient.
